contract.structural_score_basis: ⚠️ **AUTHORED 2026-09-10 at 4.0 — the first axis-5 score this asset has ever had.** security_analyst hand-walked six layers today with controls that DISCRIMINATE (four distinct hasRole patterns; a FABRICATED role false for everyone; `0x…dEaD` false throughout), and I re-read the three load-bearing claims myself on-chain rather than adopt them. All three confirmed. ✅ **WHAT ARGUES UP, AND IT IS REAL:** on Ethereum the token and vault terminate at a **48h TimelockController with a genuine floor** — `updateDelay` is `onlySelf` — behind a **4-of-6** Safe, and **DEFAULT_ADMIN was REVOKED from that Safe at block 25,094,121**, so changing role membership must itself clear 48h. **thUSD ITSELF HAS NO PAUSE FUNCTION** — no `Pausable` in verified source — so transfers cannot be frozen by anyone, which is rarer than it sounds. The pause that does exist runs **fail-safe**: halting sthUSD is instant, restarting takes 48h, so the delay runs in the holder's direction. Neither OFT adapter is upgradeable (no non-zero ERC-1967 slot), and `setPeer` was observed executing THROUGH the timelock. ⚠️⚠️ **WHAT HOLDS IT TO 4.0 IS NOT ETHEREUM — IT IS THAT THE PUBLISHED PICTURE WAS MISSING THE CHAIN THAT HOLDS THE MONEY.** Every surface, including security_analyst's walk and my own report, worked from a chain list of Ethereum + Arbitrum (+ an unread 'Stable'). **I enumerated the Ethereum adapter's LayerZero peers instead of trusting the list** — `peers(uint32)` across EIDs 30101–30400 — and found FOUR configured peers: bnb 30102, arbitrum 30110, mantle 30181, and **30396 = Stable**. **The escrow reconciles to the cent, which is what makes this safe to score on:** 51,611,845.04 thUSD locked in the Ethereum adapter = **51,416,245.78 on Stable (99.62% of all bridged thUSD) + 195,599.26 on Arbitrum (0.38%)**, with bnb and mantle configured at zero. ⚠️ **THE WEAK CONFIGURATION EVERYONE ATTRIBUTED TO ARBITRUM IS ALSO STABLE'S, AND ARBITRUM IS A ROUNDING ERROR BESIDE IT.** Measured on Stable with `0x…dEaD` false on every role: `getMinDelay` **64,800s = 18h**, Safe **3-of-5**, and the Safe **STILL HOLDS DEFAULT_ADMIN on that timelock** — so 18h is a value it can set, not a floor it must clear, and **three signatures reach it**. Same Safe address, same timelock address, three different configurations. **37.99% of Ethereum-supply-equivalent thUSD sits behind that.** ⚠️ **AND THERE IS AN UNDELAYED FULL-REACH PATH ON THE SAME CONTRACTS.** LayerZero endpoint `delegates()` returns the **governance Safe DIRECTLY — not the timelock** — for both adapters on Ethereum (4-of-6) and both OFTs on Arbitrum (3-of-5), verified with `delegates(0x…dEaD)` returning the zero address as a control. **Ownership is delayed 48h; delegation is not delayed at all**, and the delegate configures the DVN/library stack that decides whether an inbound mint message is accepted. ⚠️ **The blast radius is the adapter's escrow, not the whole float** — a forged inbound message releases what is LOCKED, i.e. up to 51.6M — but that bound is still 38% of supply and it is reachable with zero notice. ⚠️ **THREE SINGLE-KEY FACTS, none of which alone would move this, and which compound:** the ONLY address that can create thUSD is a bare EOA (`0x09ec7c2d…`, no code, nonce 328; `hasRole(MINTER_ROLE)` true for it, false for the Safe, false for `0x…dEaD`, false for a fabricated role) — **bounded** by a real published cap of 1,000,000/block, EIP-712 signatures and a whitelist, **but `setMinter` is `onlyOwner` at 48h and is FULL reach, because a replacement minter does not inherit the cap: the bound lives in the minter contract, not in the token.** A single keyed address holds **CANCELLER alone** on Ethereum and can veto any queued operation unilaterally. And **PROPOSER = CANCELLER on all three chains**, so there is no independent veto anywhere. ⚠️ **The governance Safe (4-of-6) and the reserve Safe (4-of-5) SHARE EXACTLY FOUR OWNERS, and four is the threshold of BOTH** — one set of four signatures satisfies governance AND custody, so those two render as separate controls and are not independent ones. ⚠️ **DECLARED GAPS, carried as gaps and NOT read as clean:** (1) the LayerZero delegate on **Stable is UNREAD** — `delegates()` returned nothing at the endpoint address that answers on the other two chains, **and the `0x…dEaD` control returned nothing too, so that is MY READ FAILING, not an absence of delegate**; on both chains where it IS readable it is the Safe with zero notice, so assuming either way would be unfounded. (2) `ThUSDMinter` **EMERGENCY_ROLE holders are NOT ESTABLISHED** — the contract is not `AccessControlEnumerable`, a sweep of eight candidates returned false, and `RoleGranted` logs show only the DEFAULT_ADMIN grant; **no absence is inferred**, and the feed's `minter_paused: false` is a STATE reading, not an authority reading. (3) bnb and mantle are **configured peers holding zero supply** — latent surface that can carry value without any new authorization. **WHY 4.0 AND NOT 4.5:** on the Ethereum configuration alone this is a 4.5 — 48h with a real floor, DEFAULT_ADMIN revoked, no token pause, fail-safe asymmetry. **The half point comes off for the cross-chain half**, where 38% of supply-equivalent sits behind a delay its own Safe can rewrite at a lower quorum, an undelayed full-reach delegate path exists on every readable chain, and the largest bridged leg was absent from every chain list in this repo until today.
